description: Tracked SOC skill enrichment metadata. Reference/provenance only; not loaded by runtime routing or prompt assembly.

github_reference_skills.safety_notes: Defensive brute-force workflow only; no blocking or remote-access execution steps reused.
Splunk triage workflow converted to governed evidence-review metadata only.

conditional_mitre_candidates.condition: Only when success or valid-account misuse context exists.

investigation_workflow: Scope authentication failures by user, source, host, and time window.
Confirm threshold evidence before labeling brute-force activity evidence-supported.
Pivot to success-after-failure only when successful authentication evidence exists.
Keep SPL generation and execution behind existing validation and review gates.
analyst_checklist: Validate time window and threshold.
Compare distinct users and sources.
Check whether any successful authentication followed the failures.
Review asset or account criticality before severity claims.
answer_rules: Do not claim account compromise from failed logins alone.
Mark brute force as evidence-supported only after threshold evidence exists.
SPL/execution remains review-gated.
limitations: Failed login telemetry alone does not establish credential validity.
Source IP reuse, NAT, or scanner behavior may require analyst review.

github_reference_skills.safety_notes: Used for defensive failed-to-success sequence review only.
SOP reference only; no direct Splunk execution.

investigation_workflow: Correlate failures followed by successful authentication for the same user, source, host, and time window.
Check source IP novelty where available.
Keep Valid Accounts as a candidate unless additional misuse evidence exists.
analyst_checklist: Confirm failure and success event ordering.
Review whether the source is known for the user.
Check privileged account or critical asset context.
Look for follow-on activity before compromise language.
answer_rules: State 'successful login after failures observed.'
Do not state 'compromised account' unless additional evidence exists.
T1078 remains candidate unless stronger account-misuse evidence exists.
limitations: Sequence evidence can be benign if the user retried successfully.
Novelty is optional and may be unavailable in current telemetry.

github_reference_skills.safety_notes: Header and authentication-result evidence only; no external lookups or scripts executed.

investigation_workflow: Compare sender, return-path, reply-to, and authentication results.
Inspect URL/domain, attachment, recipient, and gateway verdict evidence.
Classify wording based on combined evidence strength.
analyst_checklist: Check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment.
Review sender and reply-to mismatch.
Collect URL/domain and attachment indicators.
Confirm gateway verdict and affected recipients.
answer_rules: Do not claim phishing confirmed only from sender mismatch.
Distinguish suspicious, likely phishing, and evidence-supported phishing.
limitations: Email header anomalies may reflect forwarding or gateway behavior.
Phishing verdict needs more than a single mismatch signal.

github_reference_skills.safety_notes: Defensive event and process evidence only; no command execution.

investigation_workflow: Collect process, command line, parent process, and script block evidence.
Flag encoded command or suspicious invocation patterns as evidence, not malware verdicts.
Pivot to network and child-process activity when available.
analyst_checklist: Review event ID and script block text.
Check parent process and user context.
Identify encoded-command usage.
Look for related network connections or child processes.
answer_rules: Do not classify as malware unless malware evidence exists.
State suspicious command execution evidence and required pivots.
limitations: Administrative scripts may use PowerShell legitimately.
Encoded command is a suspicious indicator, not a standalone malware verdict.

github_reference_skills.safety_notes: Defensive frequency, jitter, and DNS evidence only; no C2 infrastructure guidance reused.

investigation_workflow: Review periodicity, jitter, outbound volume, and domain rarity together.
Associate source with user or host identity when possible.
Escalate from candidate to evidence-supported only when multiple signals align.
analyst_checklist: Measure periodicity and jitter.
Check bytes out and DNS query count.
Assess domain rarity and destination context.
Tie traffic to a host or user before impact language.
answer_rules: Do not claim C2 confirmed from periodicity alone.
Use candidate/evidence-supported wording based on multiple signals.
limitations: Periodic traffic may be benign polling or monitoring.
Parent T1071 is used unless evidence supports a specific sub-technique.

github_reference_skills.safety_notes: IR/SOP guidance only; containment and remediation require human approval.

investigation_workflow: Summarize alert type, affected asset, user, status, related alerts, and containment state.
Use SOP guidance without assigning MITRE absent alert evidence.
Require human approval for containment or remediation.
analyst_checklist: Confirm alert type and affected asset.
Collect severity policy inputs.
Review prior related alerts.
Record containment state without recommending destructive action.
answer_rules: Use IR/SOP guidance.
Do not recommend destructive containment.
Human approval required for containment/remediation.
Do not assign MITRE without alert type/evidence.
limitations: Playbook guidance depends on alert evidence supplied by the analyst or governed retrieval.
No remediation action is authorized by this enrichment.

github_reference_skills.safety_notes: Partial accept for defensive impact evidence only; reverse-engineering/decryptor workflow sections rejected.
Optional IR playbook reference; containment/remediation require HIL.

conditional_mitre_candidates.condition: Only if recovery inhibition evidence exists.

investigation_workflow: Collect file-change, process, recovery-inhibition, service-stop, and host-impact signals.
Use T1486 evidence-supported wording only when multiple impact signals align.
Require human review for containment or remediation recommendations.
analyst_checklist: Measure file rename count and extension patterns.
Identify affected paths and process name.
Check shadow copy deletion and service stop indicators.
Count impacted hosts before scope claims.
answer_rules: Do not claim ransomware from file changes alone.
Require multiple evidence signals for evidence-supported T1486.
Require HIL for containment or remediation guidance.
limitations: Bulk file changes can be benign administrative or backup activity.
This enrichment does not include malware reverse-engineering or decryptor guidance.

investigation_workflow: Scope and baseline: identify source and destination (workstation, jump server, VPN gateway, PAW, OT host, cloud console); confirm the login matches the user's normal pattern, shift, location, and device.

Account and asset context: check whether the account is privileged, dormant, service-like, or recently modified; check whether the target is crown-jewel, domain controller, OT engineering workstation, or SCADA gateway.

Authentication evidence: check repeated failures before success for the same user/source/host/time window; check multiple users from one source IP; review MFA outcome (approved, denied, timeout, push fatigue, bypass, none); validate source IP novelty against known corporate or VPN egress.

Post-authentication pivots: review first commands, processes, or administrative actions after login; check for PsExec, WMI, PowerShell remoting, RDP, SMB admin shares, or unusual remote service use; check access to sensitive shares, domain controllers, OT systems, or credential stores.
Correlate across EDR, VPN/IdP, firewall, proxy, PAM/IAM, and asset inventory before drawing conclusions.
Threat intel: check source IP reputation, VPN/Tor/hosting status, and prior internal compromise history.
If the target is OT or crown-jewel infrastructure, escalate to the IT/OT incident bridge for human review.
analyst_checklist: Confirm whether the login matches the user's normal access pattern, shift timing, location, and device.
Check whether the account is privileged, dormant, service-like, or recently modified.
Check whether the target asset is crown-jewel, domain controller, OT engineering workstation, or SCADA gateway.
Review failure-then-success ordering and whether multiple users authenticated from the same source IP.
Review the MFA outcome and whether the source IP is new for this user.
Review first post-login commands, remote service use, and access to sensitive shares or credential stores.
Escalate to the IT/OT incident bridge when the target is OT or crown-jewel infrastructure.
answer_rules: State that this checklist validates whether an admin login is expected, suspicious, or requires escalation; it does not confirm compromise by itself.
Keep T1078 Valid Accounts as a candidate when the login is suspicious but not proven malicious.
Mention T1110 brute force only when the failure pattern supports it.
Mention post-login techniques (remote services, PowerShell, credential access, collection) only when observed evidence supports them.
MITRE mappings remain candidates until supported by source-grounded evidence.
limitations: A single anomalous admin login does not confirm compromise.
Login metadata alone cannot support evidence-supported MITRE claims.
High admin activity may be scheduled maintenance, automation, or approved support activity.
No containment or account action may be performed without HIL/change approval.

conditional_mitre_candidates.condition: Only when command-line/script evidence shows interpreter abuse.

answer_rules: Do not claim malware or compromise from process execution alone.
LOLBin or encoded/download command lines are suspicious, not proof; mark execution evidence-supported only with corroborating telemetry.
Do not assert Impair Defenses (T1562.001) without direct tool/service tamper evidence.
SPL/execution remains review-gated.
analyst_checklist: Confirm process_name, parent_process, and command_line.
Check for encoded or download command-line markers.
Review host/user criticality before severity claims.
Corroborate with network or persistence signals.
investigation_workflow: Scope suspicious process executions by host, user, and time window.
Identify LOLBins and encoded/download command lines.
Pivot to parent/child lineage and network connections.
Keep SPL generation and execution behind validation and review gates.
limitations: Process execution telemetry alone does not establish malicious intent.
Legitimate admin tooling can match LOLBin patterns.

conditional_mitre_candidates.condition: Only when valid-account misuse context exists beyond off-hours timing.

answer_rules: Do not claim compromise from after-hours timing alone.
Valid-account abuse (T1078) is candidate-only without corroborating anomaly or context.
Do not assert credential dumping (T1003) from login timing.
SPL/execution remains review-gated.
analyst_checklist: Confirm user, host, source IP, and event time.
Compare against the user's normal working hours and asset criticality.
Check for concurrent failures or new-source logins.
Validate before severity claims.
investigation_workflow: Scope after-hours authentications to critical assets by user/host/time.
Compare against baseline working hours and known maintenance windows.
Pivot to source reputation and concurrent activity.
Keep SPL generation and execution behind validation and review gates.
limitations: Off-hours activity is common for shift workers, automation, and global teams.
Timing alone does not establish valid-account abuse.

conditional_mitre_candidates.condition: Only when successful VPN access follows anomalous failures with misuse context.

answer_rules: Do not claim breach from a VPN failed-login spike alone.
Spikes may be expired credentials, client misconfig, or MFA friction — not necessarily attack.
Valid-account abuse (T1078) is candidate-only; needs success-after-anomaly + context.
SPL/execution remains review-gated.
analyst_checklist: Confirm user, source IPs, and failure counts.
Distinguish single-user lockout from distributed source spread.
Check for a successful VPN login following the failures.
Validate before severity claims.
investigation_workflow: Scope failed VPN authentications per user with source spread and time window.
Separate credential/config issues from distributed guessing.
Pivot to success-after-failure and source reputation.
Keep SPL generation and execution behind validation and review gates.
limitations: Failed VPN logins alone do not establish credential validity or compromise.
NAT/shared egress can inflate source counts.

answer_rules: Do not assert intrusion or C2 from a firewall deny spike alone.
Deny spikes are frequently scanning, misconfiguration, or blocked-by-design traffic.
No MITRE technique is asserted for deny-volume alone; keep mappings not-claimed without corroborating evidence.
SPL/execution remains review-gated.
analyst_checklist: Confirm src, dest, deny_count, and destination ports.
Distinguish inbound scanning from outbound blocked traffic.
Check destination reputation and port spread.
Validate before severity claims.
investigation_workflow: Scope firewall denies per source/destination with port spread and time window.
Separate scanning/misconfig from targeted blocked activity.
Pivot to reputation and correlated host telemetry.
Keep SPL generation and execution behind validation and review gates.
limitations: Deny events represent blocked traffic; a spike is not evidence of successful compromise.
Scanning and misconfiguration are common benign causes.
